then.text: Same pint, smaller pound. Write that in your little book.

else.text: Decimal Day, 15 February 1971. I was a lad. Twelve pence to the shilling, twenty shillings to the pound, gone in a weekend.
Two hundred and forty old pence became a hundred new ones. Folk swore the shops rounded everything up.
Then the seventies. In 1975 prices went up by about a quarter in one year. Wages chased them. Nobody caught anything.
That's inflation. The pint's the same pint. It's the pound that shrinks.
If prices rise 2% a year, what does a £5 pint cost in ten years?

then.text: Spot on. Two per cent on top of two per cent, ten times over. It compounds, like interest.

else.text: About £6.10. Two per cent on top of two per cent, ten times over. It compounds, like interest.
The Bank of England aims for 2% a year. In October 2022 it hit 11.1%. I noticed. My pint noticed.

whitelocks_quiz.text: {greeting} Oldest pub in Leeds, 1715. Quiz night every night if you ask nicely.

whitelocks_regular.text: {greeting} Pull up a stool. Them mirrors are older than my granddad. So's the beer, if you believe the landlord.

then.text: Not you again. I've found a very exclusive clock tower. Enquire within. Or don't. I'll be more relaxed about it.

else.text: Psst. You look like a person of vision. I've the Deed to a lovely little lighthouse. Worth four grand easy. Yours for four hundred, cash, tonight.
Tomorrow the price doubles. Others are interested. I can't say who. It's a very exclusive set of people, all of them me.
A lighthouse for a tenth of its value. What do you do?
options: Hand over the cash before it doubles
Ask who the registered owner is
Walk away and finish your drink

then.text: He's thrilled. You are, in a way, the lesson: the deadline was there to stop you thinking.
Smart. Anyone can look up who owns a property at the land registry for a few quid, and a real seller will have nothing to hide. He suddenly remembers a meeting.
Also smart. The scam only works if you don't have time to think, so thinking time is the whole defence.

else.text: The warning lights: a price far too good, a deadline, cash only, a stranger, and no paperwork you can check.
Real sales go through a solicitor or conveyancer, take weeks, and let you sleep on it. Anyone who won't let you sleep on it is selling you something else.
(The landlord slides a Yorkshire pudding across the bar.) On the house. For listening, not for buying a lighthouse.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
